# m.options.snapshots

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The current snapshot of each requested options contract, with its greeks.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.options.snapshots(symbols, *, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None, on_error=None)
```

- [Methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`, which holds only the latest poll's rows, one row per `Symbol`
- `poll(interval, mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND)`: appends each new state of a row, identified by `Symbol`, `LastQuoteLastUpdated` and `LastTradeSipTimestamp`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows its rule under [shared arguments](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Option contracts, or `dm.ALL` for every contract. |
| [`sort`](README.md#sort) | `"ticker"`. |
| [`order`](README.md#order) | The direction of `sort`. |
| [`limit`](README.md#limit) | The most rows to return, in total. A watchlist's `fetch()` caps every request instead. |
| [`filters`](README.md#filters) | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"ticker_gte": "O:AAPL"}`. Keys: `ticker_gt`, `ticker_gte`, `ticker_lt`, `ticker_lte`, `type`. |
| [`on_error`](README.md#on_error) | What a bad symbol or row does in this call (`dm.ErrorPolicy`). |

## Plans

How recent the data is on each of Massive's plans, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Unified Snapshot (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Options Basic | Not included |
| Options Starter | 15-minute delayed |
| Options Developer | 15-minute delayed |
| Options Advanced | Real-time |
| Options Business | Real-time |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The row's instrument, as Massive's ticker. From REST `ticker`: "The ticker symbol for the asset." |
| `OptionRoot` | String | The OCC option root, read from `Symbol`: the symbol without its `O:` prefix and its last 15 characters (expiry, type, and strike), such as `SPXW` for `O:SPXW251219C06000000`. It is never mapped to the underlying: an adjusted contract keeps its own root, such as `AAPL1`. |
| `Value` | double | Value of Index. |
| `BreakEvenPrice` | double | The price of the underlying asset for the contract to break even. For a call, this value is (strike price + premium paid). For a put, this value is (strike price - premium paid). |
| `ContractType` | String | The type of contract. Can be "put", "call", or in some rare cases, "other". From the `details` object: The details for this contract. |
| `ExerciseStyle` | String | The exercise style of this contract. See this link (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Option_style) for more details on exercise styles. From the `details` object: The details for this contract. |
| `ExpirationDate` | String | The contract's expiration date in YYYY-MM-DD format. From the `details` object: The details for this contract. |
| `SharesPerContract` | double | The number of shares per contract for this contract. From the `details` object: The details for this contract. |
| `StrikePrice` | double | The strike price of the option contract. From the `details` object: The details for this contract. |
| `Error` | String | The error while looking for this ticker. |
| `Fmv` | double | Fair Market Value is only available on Business plans. It is our proprietary algorithm to generate a real-time, accurate, fair market value of a tradable security. For more information, contact us (https://massive.com/contact). |
| `GreeksDelta` | double | The change in the option's price per $0.01 increment in the price of the underlying asset. From the `greeks` object: The greeks for this contract. There are certain circumstances where greeks will not be returned, such as options contracts that are deep in the money. See this article (https://massive.com/blog/greeks-and-implied-volatility/#testing) for more information. |
| `GreeksGamma` | double | The change in delta per $0.01 change in the price of the underlying asset. From the `greeks` object: The greeks for this contract. There are certain circumstances where greeks will not be returned, such as options contracts that are deep in the money. See this article (https://massive.com/blog/greeks-and-implied-volatility/#testing) for more information. |
| `GreeksTheta` | double | The change in the option's price per day. From the `greeks` object: The greeks for this contract. There are certain circumstances where greeks will not be returned, such as options contracts that are deep in the money. See this article (https://massive.com/blog/greeks-and-implied-volatility/#testing) for more information. |
| `GreeksVega` | double | The change in the option's price per 1% increment in volatility. From the `greeks` object: The greeks for this contract. There are certain circumstances where greeks will not be returned, such as options contracts that are deep in the money. See this article (https://massive.com/blog/greeks-and-implied-volatility/#testing) for more information. |
| `FmvLastUpdated` | Instant | If Fair Market Value (FMV) is available, this field is the nanosecond timestamp of the last FMV calculation. |
| `LastMinuteOpen` | double | The open value for the minute aggregate. From the `last_minute` object: The most recent minute aggregate for this contract. |
| `LastMinuteHigh` | double | The highest value for the minute aggregate. From the `last_minute` object: The most recent minute aggregate for this contract. |
| `LastMinuteLow` | double | The lowest value for the minute aggregate. From the `last_minute` object: The most recent minute aggregate for this contract. |
| `LastMinuteClose` | double | The closing value for the minute aggreate. From the `last_minute` object: The most recent minute aggregate for this contract. |
| `LastMinuteVolume` | double | The trading volume for the minute aggregate. From the `last_minute` object: The most recent minute aggregate for this contract. |
| `LastMinuteVwap` | double | The trading volume weighted average price for the minute aggregate. From the `last_minute` object: The most recent minute aggregate for this contract. |
| `LastMinuteDecimalVolume` | String | The trading volume for the minute aggregate with decimal precision. This field provides support for fractional shares, representing volume as a decimal string where the fractional part is expressed in millionths. This field is only returned for stocks snapshots. From the `last_minute` object: The most recent minute aggregate for this contract. |
| `LastMinuteTransactions` | long | The number of transactions that took place within the minute aggregate. From the `last_minute` object: The most recent minute aggregate for this contract. |
| `LastMinuteLastUpdated` | Instant | The nanosecond timestamp of when this information was updated. From the `last_minute` object: The most recent minute aggregate for this contract. |
| `LastQuoteBidPrice` | double | The bid price. From the `last_quote` object: The most recent quote for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes quotes. |
| `LastQuoteBidSize` | double | The bid size. This represents the number of shares, or contracts for options, buyers are bidding for at the given bid price. From the `last_quote` object: The most recent quote for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes quotes. |
| `LastQuoteAskPrice` | double | The ask price. From the `last_quote` object: The most recent quote for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes quotes. |
| `LastQuoteAskSize` | double | The ask size. This represents the number of shares, or contracts for options, sellers are offering at the given ask price. From the `last_quote` object: The most recent quote for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes quotes. |
| `LastQuoteBidExchange` | long | The bid side exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/options/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. From the `last_quote` object: The most recent quote for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes quotes. |

From the `last_quote` object: The most recent quote for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes quotes. |
| `LastQuoteLastUpdated` | Instant | The nanosecond timestamp of when this information was updated. From the `last_quote` object: The most recent quote for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes quotes. |
| `LastQuoteMidpoint` | double | The average of the bid and ask price. From the `last_quote` object: The most recent quote for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes quotes. |
| `LastQuoteTimeframe` | String | The time relevance of the data. From the `last_quote` object: The most recent quote for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes quotes. |
| `LastTradePrice` | double | The price of the trade. This is the price per share of the underlying, so the total dollar value of a trade is the price multiplied by the size and by the contract multiplier, which is typically 100 shares per contract. From the `last_trade` object: The most recent trade for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes trades. |
| `LastTradeSize` | long | The size of a trade (also known as volume). From the `last_trade` object: The most recent trade for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes trades. |
| `LastTradeConditions` | long[] | A list of condition codes. The codes depend on the asset type; see the condition codes for stocks (https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/market-operations/condition-codes), options (https://massive.com/docs/rest/options/market-operations/condition-codes), or crypto (https://massive.com/docs/rest/crypto/market-operations/condition-codes). From the `last_trade` object: The most recent trade for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes trades. |
| `LastTradeDecimalSize` | String | The size of a trade, including fractional shares, represented as a decimal string where the fractional part is expressed in millionths. This field is only returned for stocks snapshots. From the `last_trade` object: The most recent trade for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes trades. |
| `LastTradeExchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/options/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. From the `last_trade` object: The most recent trade for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes trades. |
| `LastTradeId` | String | The trade ID. Options trades do not have a trade ID, so this field is returned as an empty string. From the `last_trade` object: The most recent trade for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes trades. |
| `LastTradeLastUpdated` | Instant | The nanosecond timestamp of when this information was updated. From the `last_trade` object: The most recent trade for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes trades. |
| `LastTradeParticipantTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond Exchange Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade was generated at the exchange. From the `last_trade` object: The most recent trade for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes trades. |
| `LastTradeSipTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy SIP Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the SIP received this trade from the exchange which produced it. From the `last_trade` object: The most recent trade for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes trades. |
| `LastTradeTimeframe` | String | The time relevance of the data. From the `last_trade` object: The most recent trade for this contract. This is only returned if your current plan includes trades. |
| `ImpliedVolatility` | double | The market's forecast for the volatility of the underlying asset, based on this option's current price. |
| `LastUpdated` | Instant | The nanosecond timestamp of when this information was updated. |
| `MarketStatus` | String | The market status for the market that trades this ticker. Possible values for stocks, options, crypto, and forex snapshots are open, closed, early_trading, or late_trading. Possible values for indices snapshots are regular_trading, closed, early_trading, and late_trading. |
| `Message` | String | The error message while looking for this ticker. |
| `Name` | String | The name of this contract. |
| `SessionPrice` | double | The price of the most recent trade or bid price for this asset. From the `session` object: Comprehensive trading session metrics, detailing price changes, trading volume, and key price points (open, close, high, low) for the asset within the current trading day. Includes specific changes during early, regular, and late trading periods to enable detailed performance analysis and trend tracking. Values describe the current trading session only; nothing carries over from the previous session apart from `previous_close`. For stocks snapshots, an asset that has not traded yet this session reports `volume: 0` with the price and change fields omitted rather than reported as 0. During early trading on stocks snapshots, `volume` and `price` track the session as it happens, but `open`, `high`, `low`, `close` and `vwap` are omitted until the regular session opens, as those report official session prices. They appear from the open and remain through late trading. For options snapshots, the early, regular and late trading changes use these sessions: early trading from 7:30 to 9:30 AM ET, the regular session from 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM ET (4:15 PM ET for some products, such as SPY and SPX options), and late trading from the end of the regular session to 5:00 PM ET. Only trades marked with the extended hours condition (EXHT, 248) count as early or late trading. Cboe's extended trading hours program covers selected equity options, so other contracts do not get an early or late trading change. Index options, such as SPX, SPXW and XSP, get the regular trading change only. A change field is omitted when the contract has no trade in that session on the current trading day, or when the price it is measured against is missing. A change of 0 is returned as 0. |

A change field is omitted when the contract has no trade in that session on the current trading day, or when the price it is measured against is missing. A change of 0 is returned as 0. |
| `SessionEarlyTradingChangePercent` | double | Today's early trading change as a percentage of `previous_close`. From the `session` object: Comprehensive trading session metrics, detailing price changes, trading volume, and key price points (open, close, high, low) for the asset within the current trading day. Includes specific changes during early, regular, and late trading periods to enable detailed performance analysis and trend tracking. Values describe the current trading session only; nothing carries over from the previous session apart from `previous_close`. For stocks snapshots, an asset that has not traded yet this session reports `volume: 0` with the price and change fields omitted rather than reported as 0. During early trading on stocks snapshots, `volume` and `price` track the session as it happens, but `open`, `high`, `low`, `close` and `vwap` are omitted until the regular session opens, as those report official session prices. They appear from the open and remain through late trading. For options snapshots, the early, regular and late trading changes use these sessions: early trading from 7:30 to 9:30 AM ET, the regular session from 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM ET (4:15 PM ET for some products, such as SPY and SPX options), and late trading from the end of the regular session to 5:00 PM ET. | `OpenInterest` | double | The quantity of this contract held at the end of the last trading day. |
| `Timeframe` | String | The time relevance of the data. |
| `UnderlyingAssetPrice` | double | The price of the trade. This is the actual dollar value per whole share of this trade. A trade of 100 shares with a price of $2.00 would be worth a total dollar value of $200.00. From the `underlying_asset` object: Information on the underlying stock for this options contract. The market data returned depends on your current stocks plan. |
| `UnderlyingAssetValue` | double | The value of the underlying index. From the `underlying_asset` object: Information on the underlying stock for this options contract. The market data returned depends on your current stocks plan. |
| `UnderlyingAssetChangeToBreakEven` | double | The change in price for the contract to break even. From the `underlying_asset` object: Information on the underlying stock for this options contract. The market data returned depends on your current stocks plan. |
| `UnderlyingAssetLastUpdated` | Instant | The nanosecond timestamp of when this information was updated. From the `underlying_asset` object: Information on the underlying stock for this options contract. The market data returned depends on your current stocks plan. |
| `Underlying` | String | The instrument Massive lists the row under, as Massive's ticker. From REST `underlying_asset.ticker`: "The ticker symbol for the contract's underlying asset. From the `underlying_asset` object: Information on the underlying stock for this options contract. The market data returned depends on your current stocks plan." |
| `UnderlyingAssetTimeframe` | String | The time relevance of the data. From the `underlying_asset` object: Information on the underlying stock for this options contract. The market data returned depends on your current stocks plan. |
| `Type` | String | The asset class for this ticker. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, by the local clock. Rows that arrive together share it. It isn't Massive's time, and later rows can carry earlier times. In a `poll()` table, it's the time of the poll the row's values came from. |

## Massive's documentation

- [Unified Snapshot (REST)](https://massive.com/docs/rest/options/snapshots/unified-snapshot)

---

The plan tables and most column descriptions are Massive's, from its documentation as fetched on 2026-11-09, with a few corrected where Massive's are wrong. The library writes its own descriptions of the columns it names or computes, such as `Symbol` and `TimestampInsert`.
